6 PLAYBOOKS FOR 6 DIFFERENT MARKET REGIMES

Last week’s firm-wide @smbcapital meeting was about better adapting to different market regimes.

Which begs the question - what types of market regimes are there for discretionary traders? And what playbooks should we be running for each of them?

I’ll start and you all can expand on this in the replies.

Obviously this is far from exhaustive and kept high-level, but I think this should lead serious traders to do some deep reflection of their own. 

1. Theme-driven bullish market. Markets like this one favor momentum strategies, swing longs, overnight momentum, IPOs, and headlines relevant to the driving theme.

Early summer of 2026 certainly fell under this with AI as the driver and leading sectors like DRAM / cloud computing.

2. Macro-driven markets. Think in the spring during the start of the U.S.-Iran conflict, think  2025 Trump tariffs and the Russia-Ukraine war. Due to the randomness and volatility of these headlines, this market highly favors breaking news trading as well as trading move-to-move, while greatly reducing overnight exposure and swing exposure. 

3. Range-bound market. Think of the last couple months, where we've had no prevailing theme and most indices have stayed range-bound while the leaders from the prior cycle corrected. META OFFICIALLY ENTERS THE CAPITAL RAISING GAME THROUGH SELLING MORE OF THEIR STOCK.

Meta announced plans to raise approximately $35 billion through two equity offerings:

- $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements.

- $12.5B in depositary shares tied to mandatory convertible preferred stock.

The company is also considering a separate $60 billion offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares, potentially beginning in Q1 2027. The nonvoting class was introduced on earnings last week and will result in a 2-for-1 stock split.

Capital is now becoming the constraint…whoever can raise the most will win.

بينما المقابل لهذا هو اختفاء السلع والمحروقات وعدم القدرة على توفيرها من الأساس.

احنا شوفنا في ٢٠٢٢ - ٢٠٢٣ عند بداية حرب روسيا، تثبيت سعر الصرف في البنوك خلق سوق سوداء وصلت بسعر الدولار إلى ٧٠ جنيه. ودا حرفيا مدمر للاقتصاد.

That tracks with my experience. I've written 4 non-fiction books with my wife (who graduated summa cum laude with a degree in journalism) acting as primary editor.

The first thing she ever edited for me was a piece that Barron's published in 1992. I—having been the Editor-in-Chief of my High School newspaper and a long-time writer—thought the version I gave to her only needed a bit of polishing. 

What came back from her was a SEA of red ink with innumerable corrections and rewrites. 

I was livid! Not only was my ego crushed, I turned it into a huge fight with her, accusing her of trying to drain all of my wonderfully creative darlings out of the piece and replacing them with pedestrian prose for the sake of clarity. The fight got so heated we ended up not speaking about it for the rest of the day.

But then I dutifully went through my original draft and made all of the changes she recommended and the scales fell from eyes—her edited version of my original draft was VASTLY better than my draft. I immediately confessed this to her while simultaneously begging her to be the primary editor on the first book I wrote called "Invest Like the Best."

In hindsight, this was the best thing that could have ever happened to my writing career. Yes, I was emotionally wounded by the harsh criticism, but it was clearly needed. I'm of the opinion that ALL writers, no matter how gifted, could see their work materially improved by a gifted, honest to the point of inflicting emotional damage
